mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in liquidity and an increase in borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, which leads to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS drops > 2% month-over-month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and lower corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5% in 3 months, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising housing starts (HOUST) and increasing retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 1.4 million units and RSAFS > 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS meet the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to higher consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE drops > 0.3% and PAYEMS increases > 100k in 3 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where both UNRATE and PAYEMS meet the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) indicates easing inflationary pressures, which can lead to a more accommodative monetary policy and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL decreases > 0.5% month-over-month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
